contrast: v489: noun_preposition collapsed entirely (32/32 dropped) when a competing cue noun was interposed. v475: possessive_number resisted a number attractor 32/32. Three behaviours, three outcomes -- recency dominance is behaviour-specific and is not a general property of these circuits, which qualifies the standing 'recency readers' note rather than confirming it.
instrument: CPU capability screen (g.prepare valid_only=True); the screen alone adjudicates the categorical question
observation_not_attributed: Margins fall from +/-7.0 and +/-7.3 without a correlative to +/-2.6 and +/-3.6 with the discharged one -- roughly a 60% cost. I do NOT attribute that to the discharged correlative: the two interpositions also differ in length and lexis, so the comparison confounds them. Attributing it needs a length-matched correlative-free interposition, which is a separate cell.
registered_reading: A recency reader answers from the nearest correlative, which here is a DISCHARGED either/or, on both sides -- so a capability collapse is the recency outcome. The correlative-free control in the same frame separates that from 'this frame is too heavy'.
result: NO collapse in either cell: 32/32 rows kept on both hypotheses of both cells. The model tracks the STILL-OPEN correlative, not the nearest one.
scope: Behavioural, not causal. It says what the MODEL does; it does not say what a fitted direction encodes.
